newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.74/75 per dlr, may gain.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.74/75 per dlr, may gain.

text.p: The Indian rupee closed at 35.740/750 a dollar on Thursday, down from the opening rate of 35.725/740, dealers said.
The day was marked by a slowdown in corporate demand for dollars and expectations of an intervention by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). But RBI bought no dollars on Thursday.
"Over the next week, the rupee could even gain if today's trend continues and if RBI keeps off," said a bank dealer.
On Wednesday, RBI bought dollars from several banks at 35.72/73 level, the first time it bought when rupee was weak.
Many dealers speculated the RBI was shoring up its reserves ahead of large outflows scheduled for the year-end.
Expectations that the RBI would step into the market kept the dollar firm despite a lack of large orders, dealers said.
Premia rose in the forward dollar market on the back of a sharp spurt in overnight call money rates and a firm spot dollar, dealers said.
Six month annualised premia closed at 6.83 percent, up from the previous closing of 6.44 percent, dealers said.
